idee_recherchee.texte: The Big Bang was not an explosion in space but the rapid expansion of space itself from an extremely hot and dense state about 13.8 billion years ago, and the question of what came before it remains unanswered.

titre: Faut-il s'inquiéter ? Luboš Motl et l'absence d'explosion en 13 milliards d'années
resume: Most scientists are not concerned, since the universe has not eaten itself in about 13 billion years since the Big Bang. Czech string theorist Luboš Motl argues the idea should be used to rule out certain descriptions of the universe, and scientists treat the scenario as something to rectify rather than agonize over.
texte: So, should we be concerned about bubbles of nothing appearing in space [music] and devouring the entire universe? Apparently not. Most scientists believe that since the universe hasn't eaten itself in 13 billion years since the Big Bang, it's an unlikely scenario. One Czech string theorist named Luboš Motl went so far as to say that we should use the ideas of bubbles of nothing to rule out certain descriptions of our universe. Since if it was going to happen, it would have happened by now. That doesn't totally negate the possibility, but it's also reassuring to know that scientists consider this to be something to rectify, not something to agonize over. We're not sure exactly how scientists would suggest that we fix a bubble of [music] nothing, but it's nice to know that they at least think we can, right?
